top_temples.name: Nasiyan Jain Temple (Soniji Ki Nasiyan)
top_temples.location_note: Late 19th-century Digambara Jain temple famed for its gold-plated 'Swarna Nagari' (City of Gold) hall depicting Jain cosmology.

top_temples.name: Nareli Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Modern Digambara Jain complex on the outskirts of Ajmer along the Jaipur highway, blending traditional and contemporary temple architecture.

top_temples.name: Shri Rangnath Swami Temple
top_temples.location_note: South Indian (Dravidian) style temple in the heart of Ajmer city, unusual for the region's architecture.

top_temples.name: Chamunda Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Said to be roughly 1,200 years old, linked to the Chauhan dynasty's devotion to the goddess.

top_temples.name: Ambe Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Prominent Devi shrine within Ajmer city, one of the city's well-known Hindu temples.

top_temples.name: Kiradu Temples (Someshvara Temple)
top_temples.location_note: 11th-century complex of five temples near Barmer, renowned for intricate stone carving; Someshvara is the best-preserved.

top_temples.name: Nagnechi Mata Temple, Barmer Fort
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple within Barmer Fort, site of large Navratri fairs.

top_temples.name: Devka Sun Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located in Devka village about 62 km from Barmer on the Barmer-Jaisalmer road, known for its architecture.

top_temples.name: Jagdambe Temple
top_temples.location_note: Believed to be over 500 years old, perched roughly 140 feet above ground on a hill.

top_temples.name: Nakoda Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Major Jain pilgrimage temple in Barmer district, known for its spiritual significance and architecture.

top_temples.name: Bhandasar Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: 15th-16th century Jain temple in Bikaner city, noted for marble pillars, gold-leaf walls, and mirror work.

top_temples.name: Shri Laxminath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Popular Bikaner temple drawing large crowds especially during Janmashtami.

top_temples.name: Kodamdeshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 24 km from Bikaner; site associated with the city's founding by Rao Bika.

top_temples.name: Shiv Bari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located about 6 km from Bikaner city, built by devotees as a mark of devotion to Shiva.

top_temples.name: Ratan Bihari & Rasik Shiromani Temples
top_temples.location_note: Mid-19th-century haveli-style twin temples built by Maharaja Ratan Singh, blending Rajputana and Mughal architecture.

top_temples.name: Karni Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: World-famous 'Rat Temple' near Bikaner, home to over 20,000 sacred rats (kabas); silver gates donated by Maharaja Ganga Singh.

top_temples.name: Laxman Shrine
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine within the main Karni Mata Temple complex, tied to the legend of Laxman's drowning and reincarnation as a rat; not a separate standalone temple.

top_temples.name: Eklingji Temple
top_temples.location_note: 8th-century temple complex about 22 km from Udaipur; hereditary family deity of the Mewar royal dynasty, surrounded by 108 smaller shrines.

top_temples.name: Lakulish Temple
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrine within the Eklingji temple complex, dedicated to the founder of the Pashupata Shaivite sect.

top_temples.name: Galtaji Temple (Surya Mandir / Balaji)
top_temples.location_note: Pilgrim site in the Aravalli Hills on Jaipur's edge, known for natural spring-fed water tanks (kunds); also called the Monkey Temple.

top_temples.name: Ramgopalji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Distinct temple within the same Galtaji complex, also known as part of the Galwar Bagh grounds.

top_temples.name: Birla Mandir (Laxmi Narayan Temple)
top_temples.location_note: White-marble temple at the base of Moti Dungri Hill, known for carvings of Hindu scripture scenes.

top_temples.name: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Jaipur's oldest temples, believed to fulfill wishes; especially busy on Wednesdays.

top_temples.name: Akshardham (Swaminarayan) Temple
top_temples.location_note: Known for stunning architecture and cultural exhibits, part of the Swaminarayan temple network.

top_temples.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located within the City Palace complex; one of the most revered Krishna temples in India.

top_temples.name: Shila Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1604 by Maharaja Man Singh I within Amer Fort; opens to devotees mainly during Navratri.

top_temples.name: Chamunda Mataji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located at the southern end of Mehrangarh Fort; installed as the royal deity by Rao Jodha in 1460.

top_temples.name: Maha Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 2 km from Jodhpur on Mandore road; famed for 84 intricately carved pillars depicting yoga postures.

top_temples.name: Raj Ranchhodji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1905 by Maharani Jadechi Rajkanwar; one of India's notable century-old Krishna temples.

top_temples.name: Rasik Bihari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located off Udai Mandir Street in Jodhpur, dedicated to Rasik Bihari (Krishna).

top_temples.name: Ganesh Temple, Ratnada Hill
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest temples in Jodhpur, situated atop Ratnada Hill.

top_temples.name: Khatu Shyam Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of India's most-visited Krishna-devotion pilgrimage sites, in Sikar district.

top_temples.name: Shyam Kund
top_temples.location_note: Sacred tank adjacent to the main temple, believed to be where Barbarik offered his head to Krishna; a sacred site tied to the temple rather than a separate standalone shrine, reflecting Khatu's identity as a single-shrine pilgrimage town.

top_temples.name: Khade Ganesh Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Known for its unique standing (khade) idol; especially crowded during Ganesh Chaturthi.

top_temples.name: Mathuradheesh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Belongs to the Vallabh (Pushtimarg) sect, known for its daily aarti.

top_temples.name: Kansua Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ancient temple with a four-faced Shiva lingam, traditionally linked to the Pandavas.

top_temples.name: Garadia Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple overlooking the Chambal River, surrounded by greenery.

top_temples.name: Chandreshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located near the Chambal River amid hills and trees.

top_temples.name: Dilwara Jain Temples
top_temples.location_note: 11th-13th century marble temple complex, world-famous for its intricate carving; Rajasthan's only hill station.

top_temples.name: Adhar Devi Temple (Arbuda Devi)
top_temples.location_note: Cave shrine reached via roughly 200 steps up a hillside; the goddess after whom Mount Abu (Arbuda) is named.

top_temples.name: Jain Glass Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nagaur town temple noted for its glass-mosaic interior and ornate craftwork.

top_temples.name: Dadhimati Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest surviving temples in northern India, dating to the 4th-century Gupta era.

top_temples.name: Digambar Jain Bara Temple, Ladnun
top_temples.location_note: Ladnun is a major Jain spiritual center; the temple houses 166 marble Tirthankara sculptures.

top_temples.name: Atishaya Kshetra Lunwa Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jain pilgrimage site in Lunwa village, Nagaur district, established in 1672.

top_temples.name: Pashupati Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located in Manjhwas village, Nagaur district; built in 1982 by Yogi Ganeshnath.

top_temples.name: Shrinathji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Central temple of the Pushtimarg sect; considered one of the richest temples in India after Tirupati.

top_temples.name: Charbhuja Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located on the outskirts of Nathdwara near the old Bor Rajput fort; a distinct, well-known temple from Shrinathji.

top_temples.name: Somnath Temple, Pali
top_temples.location_note: Located in the heart of Pali city; traditionally attributed to the Gujarat ruler Kumarpal Solanki.

top_temples.name: Nimbo Ka Nath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located between Falna and Sanderao in Pali district; legend ties it to the Pandavas' exile.

top_temples.name: Parshuram Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Cave temple tucked into the Aravalli hills' forests near Pali.

top_temples.name: Muchhal Mahavir Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jain temple in Pali district, near the Kumbhalgarh wildlife sanctuary.

top_temples.name: Om Banna Temple (Bullet Baba)
top_temples.location_note: Distinctive roadside folk shrine on the Pali-Jodhpur highway, unique to the region.

top_temples.name: Brahma Temple
top_temples.location_note: India's only major temple dedicated to Brahma; town also hosts the famous Pushkar Camel Fair.

top_temples.name: Savitri Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop temple overlooking Pushkar Lake, reached by a trek or ropeway.

top_temples.name: Ranakpur Jain Temple (Chaumukha/Adinath Temple)
top_temples.location_note: 15th-century marble temple famed for over 1,400 intricately carved pillars, no two alike.

top_temples.name: Surya Temple, Ranakpur
top_temples.location_note: Pre-dates the main Jain temple and was rebuilt alongside it in the 15th century; part of the same Ranakpur complex.

top_temples.name: Salasar Balaji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Major Hanuman pilgrimage site in Churu district, hugely popular across northern India.

top_temples.name: Mohan Das Ji & Kanidadi Shrine
top_temples.location_note: Shrine near the main Salasar Balaji Temple marking the footprints/samadhi of two revered devotees; an associated site rather than an independent major temple.

top_temples.name: Badri Vishal Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 450-year-old temple near Natwada, east of Tonk town; hosts an annual Akshaya Tritiya fair.

top_temples.name: Kalyanji Temple, Todaraisingh
top_temples.location_note: One of the older functioning Hindu temples in the region, located in Todaraisingh.

top_temples.name: Bisaldeo (Gokarneswar) Temple, Bisalpur
top_temples.location_note: 12th-century temple near Bisalpur, roughly 60-80 km from Tonk, known for intricate stone carving.

top_temples.name: Jaldevi Temple, Bavadi
top_temples.location_note: About 250 years old, located in Bavadi village near Todaraisingh.

top_temples.name: Charbhuja Mandir, Nagarfort
top_temples.location_note: One of several ancient temples in Nagarfort village, Tonk district, near a sacred village pond.

top_temples.name: Jagdish Temple
top_temples.location_note: Largest and most famous temple in Udaipur, within the City Palace complex; Indo-Aryan architecture.

top_temples.name: Neemach Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Perched on Devlali/Dewali Hill overlooking Fateh Sagar Lake.

top_temples.name: Mahakaleshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located on the banks of Fateh Sagar Lake.

top_temples.name: Mahalaxmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Marble temple with intricate carvings, believed to be about 400 years old.

top_temples.name: Ambika Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Considered the oldest temple in Udaipur, known for its lavish sculptures and rock-cleft base.
